newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SAUDI, VENEZUELA, IRAN, LIBYA MINISTERS TO MEET.
newsitem.headline: SAUDI, VENEZUELA, IRAN, LIBYA MINISTERS TO MEET.

text.p: The oil ministers of Saudi Arabia, Venezuela, Iran and Libya are to meet at 1000 GMT on Wednesday to discuss the issue of quota compliance, delegates said.
One Gulf source said the meeting was designed to emphasise the need for better quota compliance, but was not aimed at sending a warning to countries producing above their quotas.
"There is no warning," the source said.
Venezuela is widely seen as producing around 800,000 barrels per day above its OPEC quota of 2.359 million bpd.
"It is a question of common interests including of course Venezuela's interests," the source said.

The full OPEC ministerial conference is scheduled to open at 1400 GMT to discuss output levels for the rest of 1997. The producer group is widely expected to freeze its current 25.03 million bpd ceiling.
Saudi Arabia has no plans to produce above its 8.0 million bpd quota, the Gulf source added.
